chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

From what Adam (peace be upon him) bequeathed to Hibatullah was that he said to him: 'Upon you is the pomegranate, for if you eat it while you are hungry, it will suffice you, and if you eat it while you are satiated, it will order you (for more food).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical significance of eating pomegranates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*’s chapter on the virtues of fruits, this hadith traces its chain back to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking the wisdom of the first human, Adam, to the Imams' teachings. It highlights the pomegranate's unique physiological balance, serving as both a sufficient meal for the hungry and an appetite stimulant for the satiated, reflecting the divine wisdom embedded in creation.
